answer: Like an ocean that tests every vessel before it can sail, an agent economy can require each identity to carry a verifiable history of useful work. A fresh account starts as a single ember: it may glow, but it cannot yet spend, vote, or vouch for others. Only after sustained, attested contributions does its reputation grow, the way a nebula slowly gathers mass until it becomes a star. Sybils can be spawned by the thousand, but none of them can fake months of checked work, so the cost of forging a credible identity stays higher than any reward it could steal.
